items.heading: Freelancing Does Not Start
items.text: Freelancing does not start with a business name, a logo, or a resignation letter. It starts with proving, to yourself and to one stranger, that you can finish a real piece of work someone would pay for. Everything that follows, pricing, platforms, and eventually going full-time, only works once that first proof exists.

items.heading: A Sellable Skill
items.text: A sellable skill and an enjoyable skill are not always the same thing, and confusing the two is one of the most common reasons a freelance start goes nowhere. Before you commit weeks of effort to one direction, run it through a quick check.

items.heading: A Full Portfolio Website
items.text: A full portfolio website with a case-study format, a custom domain, and a polished "about me" page is a project for later. What actually gets you your first client is a small, honest set of proof, organized around what Future Career School calls the three proofs: Show it, Say it, and Proof of Value.

visuals.heading: Build Proof Before You Build a Portfolio

rows: Two or three finished pieces that show the actual craft: a live site, a written sample, a real dataset turned into a dashboard, a short edited video. Not a certificate. Not a course completion badge.
One clear write-up per piece: the problem, what you did, why you made that choice, and the result. Clients hire people who can explain decisions, not just execute them.

Any signal that your work changed an outcome, even a small one: a friend's Instagram page grew after your captions, a mock client brief you solved end-to-end, a freelance micro-task you completed for near-free just to get a testimonial.
